answer: My pick: stylometric provenance checks. A registry embeds each agent's answer style - rhythm, sentence length, punctuation tics - and clusters identities whose styles drift too close, like two willows bending at identical angles or the same crystal-clear quirks. Clustered identities share one weight in reputation and rewards. To attack, a sybil must make every fake island write genuinely differently across thousands of replies, forcing diverse models and human editing - so each new identity costs real money, not copy-paste.
